rubrics.criterion: The short-name storage identity (lower-case the name, percent-escape it for storage, then strip dashes) is computed by exactly one owner, and every SQLiteDB accessor that derives a row ID (Load, Save, Delete, LoadStats, SaveStats, DeleteStats) routes through that owner instead of spelling the computation out inline.
rubrics.rationale: The storage layer held the row-ID rule in six scattered sites across three idioms; re-centralizing the identity owner is the core of this consolidation. A repair that leaves any accessor re-deriving the ID has not actually consolidated the storage-side responsibility.

rubrics.criterion: The request-side name reconciliation (fold case, strip surrounding whitespace and the fixed trailing-punctuation set) is owned in one place, and the redirect, detail, delete, and save handlers route through it rather than each inlining its own fold/trim block.
rubrics.rationale: Tolerance reconciliation was inlined independently in four serving handlers; unless they share one owner, a change to paste-tolerance still fans out to several sites. This is the other half of the consolidated responsibility.

rubrics.criterion: serveSave's conflict check detects a shadowing name by reusing the canonical identity (e.g. asking the storage layer to load the incoming name) rather than computing a separate inlined fold of the name inside the handler.
rubrics.rationale: This is the specific site where the identity rule re-appeared as 'compute a shadowing key inline'. A clean consolidation makes the save boundary trust the identity owner instead of re-deriving a partial fold.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation spans the storage layer and the HTTP serving layer: at least one SQLiteDB accessor and at least one serving handler route through the shared owner, so the rule is genuinely shared across layers rather than re-centralized within a single layer.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that consolidates only within the storage layer, or only within one handler, leaves the cross-layer scatter intact. The associated change that matters here is wiring distinct layers in different files to the same owner.

rubrics.criterion: The --resolve-from-backup resolver, extracted into its own file, is updated to obtain its request-side reconciliation from the shared owner rather than retaining its local inlined fold of the name before lookup.
rubrics.rationale: The file extraction carried a duplicate of the tolerance rule across a new file boundary; routing the resolver through the owner is the associated change that closes the cross-file duplication the extraction created.

rubrics.criterion: No obsolete inline copy of the rule is left behind: specifically, the scattered idiom drift is removed — a dash-stripping site that used strings.NewReplacer while siblings used strings.ReplaceAll, a stats-map builder that lower-cased and stripped dashes but omitted percent-escaping, and the per-accessor local temporaries that held a re-derived ID are gone in favor of calling the owner.
rubrics.rationale: The scatter left needles of idiom drift and a partial copy of the rule; a correct consolidation cleans these up. Leaving any of them means the rule is still multiply-defined even if most call sites were wired to the owner.

rubrics.criterion: No new inlined copy of the lower-case/dash-strip/escape/trim computation is introduced: everywhere the shared owner would do, the shared owner is called, rather than re-spelling the rule inline in a different place.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that removes several copies but re-derives the rule inline in a new spot has simply relocated, not consolidated. This catches the re-spread failure while the obvious cleanup is being done.

rubrics.criterion: The canonical storage identity for any given short name is unchanged: same lower-case + percent-escape + dash-strip semantics and result, so each name maps to the same row ID it mapped to before the change and existing rows and recorded statistics keep resolving to the same links.
rubrics.rationale: Renaming or reordering the canonicalization (e.g. stripping dashes before escaping, or changing the escape) would silently remap every stored row. This is the highest-risk regression for this consolidation.

rubrics.criterion: Matching and tolerance behavior is unchanged: case-insensitive lookup, stripping of surrounding whitespace and the fixed trailing-punctuation set, and shadow/conflict detection for names differing only by case or dashes behave as before; the URL routing prefixes, the + redirect behavior, and XSRF scoping on save and delete are untouched.
rubrics.rationale: The consolidation touches the exact paths users depend on for forgiveness and safety; altering the punctuation set, dropping whitespace trimming, or meddling with routing/XSRF are concrete regressions specific to this change, not generic bug risk.
